title: Appended notes, second sequence

claims.text: Sector safety changes with regulation, technology and capital requirements; historical utility stability cannot be assumed permanent.

Reject dividing per-share working capital by shares outstanding a second time. Calculate company-level assets less the specified liabilities and divide once, distinguishing working capital from net current asset value.

Reject evaluating a convertible bond's recovery of cost solely through coupons and conversion. Contractual principal repayment, credit risk and call terms are essential to its valuation even if conversion is unlikely.
A price can remain above estimated value for a long time; valuation alone does not identify when a short position can profit or whether it can survive interim losses.
Preserve differing fiscal windows and acquisition adjustments when comparing companies. A deliberately chosen nine-month result cannot be compared as if it were a full year.
The editor explicitly disputes the claimed special economic benefit of stock dividends; corporate-action unit changes do not create wealth by themselves.

assimilation: Use the notes to correct mechanics and preserve the limits of comparative examples. Corporate-action adjustments, principal redemption, source publication and fiscal coverage are part of evidence integrity. Keep dated legal and market descriptions outside current execution rules.
adversarial_review: The bond-discount note speculates that LTV bought discounted bonds; it does not establish this from accounting disclosures, and an asset worth less than estimated does not thereby become a liability. Acquisition-failure generalizations omit successful acquirers. A quiet Y2K transition after costly remediation does not establish that the original risk was imaginary. The dividend and shareholder-voting discussion switches between share ownership percentages and numbers of people; it cannot infer an exact fraction of individuals who abstain. Hypothetical convertible-index returns exclude fees, and a blanket two-point haircut is an estimate. A stock above zero before bankruptcy does not prove bankruptcy was unforeseeable. Printed prices, returns and market capitalization may use different split conventions; do not mix them. Historical research favoring value is not a guarantee of future dominance or a substitute for this Character's test.
memory_delta: Check units once, include contractual redemption, preserve fiscal and split conventions, and separate per-person from per-share statistics. Valuation does not supply short-sale timing, past sector stability is conditional, and acquiring businesses is not inherently destructive.
